newsitem.title: GERMANY: Economists - German tax talk failure is no surprise.
newsitem.headline: Economists - German tax talk failure is no surprise.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier on Wednesday that talks between the coalition government and the opposition Social Democrats on tax reform had collapsed.
Economists said the news, while not surprising, was unfortunate for sentiment in Germany and would lengthen the period of uncertainty on the country's tax policy.
Following is a selection of economists' comments,
HOLGER FAHRINKRUG, ECONOMIST AT UBS IN FRANKFURT

"This is not a great surprise. I would have been very surprised if there had been a break through on these talks today. The government will continue to try to push this through the legislative process, but the chances are very slim indeed that the reform will come through as it stands."
HOLGER SCHMIEDING, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH IN FRANKFURT

"This is no big surprise. The economic implications are, as Theo Waigel has pointed out, that we now have even more uncertainty about tax policy, which will be bad for business confidence and investment. It is a slight dampener to hopes for a nice upswing in the economy."
ADRIAN SCHMIDT, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST AT CHASE IN LONDON

"This makes things very difficult for the government if they want to push through some austerity measures this year. It may also be negative for Germany's economic recovery because the tax reform and the tax regime are now so uncertain, but that is really sentiment driven.

"More important is whether there will be austerity measures this year to force the deficit down to EMU levels. And with them unable to agree on tax reforms, it is going to be difficult for the government to get the SPD's agreement on austerity measures."
KLAUS BAADER, SENIOR CURRENCY ECONOMIST AT DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL IN LONDON

"The immediate impact of the news will be limited, but on the whole, it will have a negative longer-term effect on sentiment. There was already quite a lot of talk in the market that Germany was really having a terrible time taking some of the more dificult steps towards reforming and making sustainable the social market economic system. So from that perspective, this is certainly not going to to German assets any favours."
